HOSPITAL KNOWLEDGE BASE — SYNTHETIC RAG DATASET

This folder contains fictional/assumed hospital documents created only for a multi-document RAG practice project.
They are NOT official documents of any hospital.

Folders:
01_Admissions
02_Departments
03_Emergency
04_Hospital
05_Patient_Safety

Each folder contains multiple documents so the RAG system can retrieve information from different files.

02 Hospital Visitor Policy
SYNTHETIC PRACTICE DOCUMENT — NOT AN OFFICIAL HOSPITAL POLICY
Version: 1.0 | Purpose: Multi-document RAG testing
Visitor Access
Visitors may enter designated patient areas according to assumed hospital visiting arrangements.
Identification
Visitors may be asked to provide identification or follow ward access procedures.
Patient Privacy
Visitors should respect patient privacy and should not access confidential records.
Restricted Areas
Clinical, pharmacy, laboratory, and other controlled areas may require authorization.
Safety
Visitors must follow staff instructions during emergencies and infection-control situations.

01 Hospital Operations Manual
SYNTHETIC PRACTICE DOCUMENT — NOT AN OFFICIAL HOSPITAL POLICY
Version: 1.0 | Purpose: Multi-document RAG testing
Purpose
This synthetic manual provides general assumed operating information for a hospital knowledge-base demonstration.
Operating Structure
The hospital operates through clinical, administrative, financial, technical, and support departments.
Patient Flow
A typical patient journey may include registration, assessment, diagnostics, treatment, admission or discharge, and billing.
Communication
Departments communicate through approved hospital systems and documented escalation channels.
Confidentiality
Patient and employee information should only be accessed by authorized personnel for legitimate work purposes.
Incident Management

Confidentiality
Patient and employee information should only be accessed by authorized personnel for legitimate work purposes.
Incident Management
Safety, clinical, security, and operational incidents should be documented through the relevant reporting process.

01 Admissions Policy
SYNTHETIC PRACTICE DOCUMENT — NOT AN OFFICIAL HOSPITAL POLICY
Version: 1.0 | Purpose: Multi-document RAG testing
Purpose
This synthetic practice policy explains the assumed admission workflow for a hospital knowledge-base demonstration.
Registration
Admissions staff verify patient identity, contact information, referral details, and the reason for admission.
Admission Order
The relevant clinical team confirms that an admission is required before the patient is assigned to an inpatient area.
Bed Assignment
The admissions desk checks available beds and coordinates placement with the receiving ward.
Required Documentation
Admission forms, consent documents where applicable, identification information, and relevant referral documents are recorded.
Handover

Admission forms, consent documents where applicable, identification information, and relevant referral documents are recorded.
Handover
The receiving department is informed when the patient is transferred to the assigned area.

02 Admission Checklist
SYNTHETIC PRACTICE DOCUMENT — NOT AN OFFICIAL HOSPITAL POLICY
Version: 1.0 | Purpose: Multi-document RAG testing
Patient Identification
Confirm the patient's name, identification details, and medical record number.
Administrative Details
Record contact information, emergency contact, payer or billing information where applicable.
Clinical Information
Confirm the admission request and relevant clinical documentation.
Bed and Ward
Confirm bed availability and communicate the assigned ward to the patient and receiving team.
Completion
Check that required admission forms have been completed before closing the admission task.

01 Emergency Department SOP
SYNTHETIC PRACTICE DOCUMENT — NOT AN OFFICIAL HOSPITAL POLICY
Version: 1.0 | Purpose: Multi-document RAG testing
Purpose
This synthetic SOP describes an assumed emergency department workflow for RAG practice.
Arrival
Patients arriving at the emergency department are registered or identified according to the emergency registration process.
Initial Assessment
Clinical staff perform an initial assessment to determine urgency and immediate care needs.
Triage
Patients are prioritized according to the assumed emergency triage procedure.
Treatment
Patients receive appropriate emergency assessment and treatment by authorized clinical staff.
Disposition
After assessment, the patient may be discharged, observed, admitted, or transferred according to the clinical decision.

Disposition
After assessment, the patient may be discharged, observed, admitted, or transferred according to the clinical decision.
Documentation
Emergency assessment, treatment, and disposition information is recorded in the patient record.

02 Emergency Escalation Guide
SYNTHETIC PRACTICE DOCUMENT — NOT AN OFFICIAL HOSPITAL POLICY
Version: 1.0 | Purpose: Multi-document RAG testing
Critical Patient
A critically ill patient should be immediately escalated to the responsible emergency clinician and relevant clinical team.
Diagnostic Support
Laboratory and radiology services may be requested when clinically required.
Admission
Patients requiring inpatient care are referred to the admissions process after the clinical decision.
Transfer
If the required service is unavailable, the responsible clinical team follows the hospital transfer procedure.

01 Patient Safety Policy
SYNTHETIC PRACTICE DOCUMENT — NOT AN OFFICIAL HOSPITAL POLICY
Version: 1.0 | Purpose: Multi-document RAG testing
Purpose
This synthetic policy establishes assumed patient-safety practices for a RAG demonstration.
Patient Identification
Staff should use appropriate identifiers before medication administration, specimen collection, procedures, and transfers.
Medication Safety
Medication orders should be checked against patient information and the authorized clinical order.
Fall Prevention
Patients identified as having a fall risk should receive appropriate precautions and monitoring.
Communication
Important changes in patient condition should be communicated promptly to the responsible clinical team.
Incident Reporting

Communication
Important changes in patient condition should be communicated promptly to the responsible clinical team.
Incident Reporting
Patient-safety incidents and near misses should be reported through the approved reporting process.

02 Incident Reporting SOP
SYNTHETIC PRACTICE DOCUMENT — NOT AN OFFICIAL HOSPITAL POLICY
Version: 1.0 | Purpose: Multi-document RAG testing
Immediate Response
Staff should first address immediate patient safety needs and notify the responsible clinical team.
Report
The incident should be documented with the date, location, people involved, and factual description.
Review
The relevant department reviews the event and identifies immediate corrective actions.
Escalation
Serious or high-risk incidents are escalated to Patient Safety and appropriate hospital leadership.
Follow-up
The safety team may review trends and recommend preventive measures.

01 Hospital Department Guide
SYNTHETIC PRACTICE DOCUMENT — NOT AN OFFICIAL HOSPITAL POLICY
Version: 1.0 | Purpose: Multi-document RAG testing
Purpose
This synthetic guide describes assumed hospital departments for testing a multi-document RAG system.
Admissions
Handles patient registration, admission coordination, and related administrative processing.
Emergency Department
Provides initial assessment and urgent care for patients requiring emergency services.
Pharmacy
Handles medication preparation, dispensing, storage, and pharmacy-related queries.
Laboratory
Processes diagnostic specimens and laboratory testing.
Radiology
Coordinates diagnostic imaging services and imaging reports.
Nursing
Provides nursing care, monitoring, documentation, and shift handover.
Finance

Coordinates diagnostic imaging services and imaging reports.
Nursing
Provides nursing care, monitoring, documentation, and shift handover.
Finance
Handles billing, payments, refunds, and financial records.
Human Resources
Handles employee records, recruitment, leave, attendance, and workplace matters.
Patient Safety and Quality
Coordinates incident reporting, safety monitoring, and quality improvement.

02 Department Responsibilities
SYNTHETIC PRACTICE DOCUMENT — NOT AN OFFICIAL HOSPITAL POLICY
Version: 1.0 | Purpose: Multi-document RAG testing
Patient Services
Supports registration, patient inquiries, complaints, and administrative coordination.
Clinical Departments
Provide specialty-specific patient assessment and treatment according to hospital procedures.
Support Services
Includes areas such as laboratory, radiology, pharmacy, facilities, and information technology.
Escalation
Questions should be directed to the department responsible for the relevant service.
